title: fix(database): use canonical CLI JSON failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Database commands emit a string-valued `error` on operational failures, so scripts cannot use the documented CLI-wide JSON failure contract.

## User Impact

Failed JSON-mode database commands return `ok: false` and `error.type: "cli_error"` with exit status 1. Successful payloads, human diagnostics, and ownership/custody checks retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared database error writer now uses `formatCliJsonFailure`, the canonical owner of CLI failure output. No second renderer, new error boundary, schema change, or config option is introduced.

Original fix and native proof by @Leon-SK668. Co-authored-by: Leon-SK668 <0668001470@xydigit.com>

## Evidence

Current-main regression: the two Gateway/embedded-agent refusal cases fail with the old string-valued error; both successful claim controls pass. With the fix, the same cases assert the canonical envelope and retain database/WAL/SHM preservation and subsequent owner-write checks. The import-boundary test also verifies that database registration does not eagerly load operation/schema runtimes.

Local commands: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-cliinput OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/database-ownership.process.test.ts src/cli/program/register.database.import-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Baseline `6d808362dd8a4853317fafef764b92ec2dac21bc`: the intended two refusal cases fail; two claim controls and the import-boundary test pass (133.53s wrapper wall time). Integrated candidate: all five tests pass (199.55s wrapper wall time, ownership suite 163.30s including cold compilation; test bodies 8.9–12.9s each). This extends the existing process fixture because in-process helper tests would miss CLI output/exit behavior and live ownership preservation. Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and diff check pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Changed-file checks passed the structural/boundary ratchets, then refused local typechecking because compiler dependencies resolve to the shared worktree installation. Their later full-tree dead-export scan reported unchanged main export `createScenarioCommandEnvironment` in the Telegram e2e script; broad scans were stopped to respect local scope. Exact-head CI is green for `f8a046ad8961d281275d770b5bf4ae59b3eea864`: [run 40247047096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40247047096), including the CI gate and actual type/lint checks. The unrelated local dead-export finding did not fail this CI run. Final-head ClawSweeper review is clean (2026-10-26 00:02 UTC).

Contributor native proof on Linux/Node 24.22.1 used the same built-CLI driver on base `f9ddc22f7a8be8d73fd88b1c24f5bf0d9348ffdd` and candidate `216551373cf1c36f7f5512d0140b448d1c931417`, with separate temporary home/state/config. Eight process cases covered canonical ownership, restore-path and preservation-locator refusals; byte-identical human ownership diagnostics; fresh/unmodified ownership status; and a legitimate external-manager claim with independent SQLite readback. For example, a claim without external-supervisor mode exited 1 on both: base returned `{"error":"Claiming external shared-state ownership requires OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external."}`, candidate returned the same message inside the canonical envelope. Driver SHA-256: `4a141df00c62b4cc5793eec7db7fa1c5e9a222ac365fbfef92c4ef874963fa5e`.

No fresh built-CLI live run was performed after integration on this loaded Mac; the contributor proof is retained and attributed, and the current-main process regression supplies the new boundary proof. Actual database port/restore, PostgreSQL, production services, and cross-platform behavior were not live-tested; this patch only changes failure rendering.

Production +3/-3 (net 0); tests +5/-2 (net +3). Simplification removes the private JSON envelope while retaining the existing error owner and process fixture.
